clinicalPearls: Caused by mutations in MYH7 encoding slow or beta-cardiac myosin heavy chain, typically within the distal light-meromyosin rod domain.
The pathological hallmark is subsarcolemmal hyaline bodies of accumulated slow myosin that are eosinophilic on haematoxylin and eosin and stain strongly for slow-myosin ATPase.
Weakness ranges from a scapuloperoneal to a limb-girdle distribution, often with prominent scapular and foot-dorsiflexor involvement.
Cardiomyopathy, whether hypertrophic or dilated, may coexist because of the shared MYH7 gene and warrants active surveillance.
Inheritance is usually autosomal dominant, with recessive and de novo cases described.
Onset ranges from childhood to adulthood, with generally slow progression.
Clinically and genetically it overlaps with Laing distal myopathy and MYH7-related cardiomyopathies.
reference.pathophysiology: MYH7 encodes the slow beta-myosin heavy chain expressed in type 1 skeletal fibres and in myocardium. Mutations, frequently in the rod domain, impair thick-filament assembly and stability, so myosin aggregates into hyaline bodies within type 1 fibres and sarcomeric contraction is disrupted. Because the same isoform is expressed in the heart, a cardiomyopathy may accompany the skeletal phenotype.
additionalInvestigations: Muscle biopsy with slow-myosin immunostaining and electron microscopy
Electrocardiography and echocardiography, with cardiac MRI if needed
Muscle MRI to define the selective involvement pattern
redFlags: New arrhythmia, syncope or symptoms of heart failure
Family history of sudden cardiac death
reference.prognosis: Skeletal weakness is generally slowly progressive with ambulation preserved for many years. The overall outlook is strongly influenced by any associated cardiomyopathy, making cardiac surveillance essential.
pitfalls: Failing to screen for and monitor cardiomyopathy.
Mistaking hyaline bodies for other protein aggregates without slow-myosin immunostaining.
Overlooking the clinical overlap with Laing distal myopathy.
Not offering cascade cardiac and neurological screening to relatives.
references: Dubowitz V, Sewry CA, Oldfors A. Muscle Biopsy: A Practical Approach
International consensus guidance on the congenital myopathies
management: Undertake cardiac surveillance with electrocardiography and echocardiography, adding cardiac magnetic resonance imaging as needed, for MYH7-related hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy and treat heart failure or arrhythmia accordingly
Maintain muscle function and mobility with physiotherapy and ankle-foot orthoses for foot-drop
Provide occupational therapy and aids for scapular and scapuloperoneal weakness
Monitor respiratory function and support with non-invasive ventilation if weakness progresses
Confirm the diagnosis by MYH7 sequencing and correlate the genotype
Offer genetic counselling for the usually autosomal dominant inheritance and cardiac screening of relatives
Coordinate care through neuromuscular and cardiology specialists
